{"explanation":"Miami's inventory has plummeted 20.4% year-over-year, driven by a sharper contraction in new listings (-14.1%) than the decline in homes sold (-8.7%). While mortgage rates have risen to 7.03% from 6.34% over the past nine months, likely dampening both buyer demand and seller activity, the supply-side pressure is the primary driver. Among Miami's regional peers, the inventory decline is steeper than the peer median of -8.6%, with North Port (-25.3%) showing comparable pressure. Months of supply contracted to 7.7 months from 8.8 months year-over-year, tightening market conditions. This inventory decline is historically unusual for Miami—similar episodes searched found no precedent in the past 36 months, making this contraction significantly sharper than prior patterns.","cited_metrics":["inventory","new_listings","homes_sold","months_of_supply"]}

{"explanation":"Pittsburgh's 7.8% median price increase to $275,000 significantly outpaces peers (median 1.8% YoY) and the nation (2.2%), driven by relatively tight inventory and strong recent demand.
